title: For every fixed c, s(k^2-c) = k for all large k, with an explicit constant (preprint)
description: Licences in this single record: the preprint (paper/paper.pdf, paper/paper.tex) is licensed under CC BY 4.0; the programs and data (code/, data/) under the MIT License, which is the licence shown for the record. Preprint with verification programs. For every fixed c, s(k^2-c) = k for all sufficiently large k, where s(n) is the side of the smallest square containing n non-overlapping unit squares. Explicitly: every packing of N unit squares in [0,k]^2 that are pairwise disjoint as closed sets has k^2 - N >= 0.0353 log k for every integer k >= 2, and k^2 - N >= (0.0657 - o(1)) log k as k -> infinity (0.0319 log k without the computer-assisted Lemma 4.10). Lemma 4.10 is a branch-and-bound computation re-verified in Arb ball arithmetic; its programs, data and logs are included. Version 1.1 added two independent checks that the accepted boxes cover the parameter domain. Version 1.2 also uses the lines near the sides, which improves the constant from 0.033 to 0.0353 and the asymptotic slope from 0.0331 to 0.0657. A new Corollary 1.3 records that, if one also uses the computer-assisted, not yet refereed result s(k^2-3) = k for all k >= 6 of E. Daniel, the constant for every k >= 2 becomes 0.0541; the main theorem does not use that result. Version 1.2 also revises several passages after an AI review of version 1.1 by the Squares Project (J. Levy), without changing the results, and fixes two scripts. Use of AI: developed with extensive assistance from Claude (Anthropic), including the proofs, the text, the programs and the computation for Lemma 4.10; the author takes full responsibility. Not peer reviewed.
